correctness.rationale: The stated all-step contraction equivalence for every nonempty graph is false if nonempty means having a vertex, as allowed by the stated connected graph scope: on the one-vertex graph L=0 and M=I even for s<1/4. The equivalence holds precisely on the nonzero-Laplacian class: the spectral decrement is (2/s)x/(1+x)^2, attaining 1/(2s) when h=2/(s lambda) for any positive eigenvalue lambda. The principal positivity claim itself checks out. Independently differentiating the path resolvent from tridiagonal continuants (H_z=-z d[(I+zL)^(-1)]/dz) reproduces all off-diagonal classes on P2, P3 and P4; K3 follows from L=3(I-P_constants), and the singleton is immediate. The only off-diagonal sign change on P4 has numerator z(z+1)(2z^3-6z^2-5z-1), with one positive zero 3.7101505426193419…; spectral calculus gives H_z,ii<=1/4 and therefore nonnegative diagonals for s>=1/2. The strict negativity beyond the cutoff follows for all s>0, without claiming sufficiency below it when s<1/2. The frozen script was inspected, not executed; the independent continuant replay is /tmp/opencode/frozen-review-replay.py, function graph_filter, and supplements the analytic sign argument.
